name: Cognizant
key_signal: CTSH has cratered ~48% over six months to a 9.7x trailing / 7.2x forward P/E, trading well below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages despite still-positive revenue and earnings growth.
thesis: At 7.2x forward earnings, 1.4x book value, and a ~3% dividend yield, CTSH is priced for much worse than the fundamentals show: gross margins of 33.5%, operating margins of 15.6%, ROE near 15%, and revenue still growing 5.8% y/y. The recent MACD histogram turning positive and RSI sitting near neutral (49.8) after a brutal 126-day drawdown (-47.7%) suggest the selling pressure may be exhausting itself, and with 25 analysts still rating it a 'buy,' sell-side consensus has not abandoned the name even as the stock has been de-rated to a valuation multiple far below typical IT services peers (which often trade 15-20x). A stabilization here could set up a mean-reversion trade back toward the 50-day SMA of $47.7.
bear_case: The technical picture is unambiguously broken — price sits below both the 50-day ($47.74) and 200-day ($64.39) moving averages with no golden cross, and a 47.7% six-month decline is not a garden-variety pullback but a regime change that the market is pricing correctly. Annualized volatility of 54.5% for a supposedly defensive IT services stock signals the market sees real fundamental risk, and the reported debt-to-equity of 7.25x (if accurate) implies a much more leveraged balance sheet than investors associate with Cognizant, which could constrain capital return (dividends, buybacks) if earnings growth continues decelerating from 3.6%. With 25 analysts already covering the name, any information edge from 'cheap valuation' has likely already been priced in by professionals who nonetheless watched the stock keep falling — a classic value trap where low P/E reflects justified expectations of further margin or growth erosion in a highly competitive, pricing-pressured IT consulting industry.
